diagnostics.message: `local_file.private_ssh_key` declares `depends_on = ["tls_private_key.ssh"]`, but the dependency is already established implicitly because `content` directly references `tls_private_key.ssh.private_key_pem`. The explicit depends_on is redundant and can be removed.

`local_file.public_ssh_key` declares `depends_on = ["tls_private_key.ssh"]`, but the dependency is already established implicitly because `content` directly references `tls_private_key.ssh.public_key_openssh`. The explicit depends_on is redundant and can be removed.

The `aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token` is created by Terraform with value "null" and `ignore_changes` on `value`; the runner instance's user-data script is responsible for writing the actual registration token into it (per the source comment "Parameter value is managed by the user-data script"). The user-data script overwrites an existing parameter (`aws ssm put-parameter ... --overwrite`), which fails if the parameter does not yet exist. Since the autoscaling group boots the instance as soon as it is created and neither an attribute reference nor a depends_on ties it to the SSM parameter, the instance can start and fail its user-data registration before the parameter is created.

When CloudWatch logging is enabled, the runner instance's user-data (data.template_file.logging / user_data) configures the awslogs agent for the log group named after the environment — the same log group Terraform creates via `aws_cloudwatch_log_group.environment`. If the autoscaling group creates the instance before the log group exists, the awslogs agent will auto-create the log group itself, causing a name collision with (or a failed create of) the Terraform-managed `aws_cloudwatch_log_group.environment`. There is no attribute reference or depends_on ensuring the log group is created before the instance boots.
